correspondence_rules: Every view concern must identify a declared requirement.
Every relationship endpoint and view component must resolve to an existing component/path.

decisions.title: Separate standalone core acceptance from later Original Blue integration

decisions.alternatives: Keep the generic speed cap and relax the original stop fixture; retain two copies of the source speed parameter; compute source collision inputs after damping may zero them.

Full f32 API/domain, contacts, dynamic orientation, supported platform and required proof coverage remain open.
decisions.decision: Generate DestinyMaxVelocity from the existing scalar component declaration and route parameter storage, access and optional replication through it. Independent original C++ case 6 additionally showed that pre-collision zeroing on exponential underflow lost finite displacement.
decisions.title: Separate the source speed parameter and preserve pre-integration collision inputs

decisions.alternatives: Keep zero acceleration while aligning; handwrite a separate warp steering implementation; treat a passing alignment fixture as all warp behavior.
decisions.consequences: All ten original positions and per-step Warp mode assertions pass in the direct Rust scenario. Proper-warp/activation event semantics, transition domains, source field side effects and required proofs remain open.
decisions.decision: Extract the existing reviewed OriginalMode::Warp negative effect-stamp guard and combine it with the actual Goto dispatch condition. Reuse the current original_goto_thrust, source collision and integration paths.
decisions.rationale: Original EvolveWarp delegates to EvolveGoto before proper warp. The original and direct Rust ten-step traces exposed missing alignment acceleration at the first step.
decisions.title: Route aligning warp through source goto thrust

decisions.alternatives: Keep missing missile acceleration or a fixed 1000ms/friction projection; duplicate the missile controller by hand.
decisions.consequences: Original launch/20-step/collider assertions, 42 scoped source transitions and future snapshot replay pass. Full interaction/target-loss/callback/configuration domains and required refinement remain open.

decisions.alternatives: Keep synthetic metadata; special-case label zero; duplicate source numeric or collision engines.

decisions.decision: Extend Tracking with separate keep-alive registration and group membership using source-bound typed rules. Cache dead free entities before control; skip source phases and temporarily project those entities to static rigid bodies for the existing Avian schedule. Re-read liveness for proximity and preserve the final check/clear.

decisions.alternatives: Zeroed candidate defaults, a second force map, copied collision algorithms or a bounded projection as the runtime owner.

decisions.decision: Generate one Forces value in each existing ball metadata owner, with lossless binary64 logical snapshot representation. Reset on actual live/free control admission, retain computed controller output, project real forces for all collision candidates and commit solver mutations including dead neighbours. Remove the redundant PreparedMotion acceleration field.

decisions.title: Retain source controller and collision forces in the existing ball metadata

decisions.alternatives: Using Avian CollidingEntities, deduplicating IDs, inventing static IDs, or queueing all collision callbacks after full-world publication.
decisions.consequences: Six direct headless witnesses cover C++ warp bits, 130 sorted original Potential contacts, old/full snapshots, source admission reset/retention and real iterative location identity zero. Missile publication/dispatch continuation, full source locations/history and mandatory proofs remain open.
decisions.decision: Generate mCollisions in the existing metadata owner and full logical snapshots. Reset at live/free behavior admission; preserve ordered kernel gradient IDs before angular updates. Project iterative location IDs separately in the existing derived Frame resource.
decisions.rationale: Source CalculateYawPitchRoll reads mCollisions, while iterative locations are appended only for moved missiles after angle update and partition reinsertion. An actual failing runtime test exposed different yaw/pitch caused by unrelated Avian contact flags.
decisions.title: Keep source contact IDs distinct from Avian contacts and iterative locations

decisions.alternatives: Prebuilding a whole event payload list, deduplicating IDs, sharing a global cursor, serializing f64 through JSON on the typed core path, or substituting an end-of-tick event drain for per-body publication.
decisions.consequences: Six independent C++ cases yield 319 contacts and three host-error notices, including same-owner recursive dispatch. Typed real-gradient output, nesting, foreign-world/owner replacement and unsafe-list-shrink handling have headless witnesses. Automatic missile publication/FFI wiring and mandatory proof/host/lifetime correspondence remain open.
decisions.decision: Generate a typed CollisionPass that captures vector size and source owner identity once. next_source_collision rereads current IDs/LastC for every notice. dispatch_source_collisions drives that same cursor and emits immediate typed host-error notices while continuing after a false host result.
decisions.rationale: A copied event batch would lose force/ID mutations and nested calls. The unchanged C++ dispatcher shows appended contacts are outside the current captured count, while recursive dispatch captures its own count and observes current data.
decisions.title: Use one operation-owned collision cursor for typed source dispatch

views.description: Latest Original Destiny is pinned independently of the Rust development branch. Prior Rust was preserved through a verified fast-forward. Source/file inventories and all 532 original cases remain visible; a complete feature denominator is not established. The current milestone is the complete standalone world engine. No complete typed host API, full state/effect denominator or production-ready acceptance is claimed; Original Blue integration remains planned.
views.name: Architecture overview

views.description: Consumers build the tracked generated adapter with ordinary locked Cargo dependencies. Clang, Doxygen and Genco are maintainer tools. The original C++ header is used only by the independent oracle. Existing specification crate math is production-reachable through the new adapter.
views.name: Component and dependency view

views.description: Distance getters read Bevy World Position components without advancing the clock. Evolve uses explicit fixed timesteps and App::update. The swept-bounds system runs in PhysicsSchedule after Avian UpdateAabbs and before CollectCollisions. Physics transform synchronization is disabled. Original controller/collision correspondence and the complete callback ordering relation remain separate unresolved obligations. Uncloak copies the source-backed proper-warp condition through a recorded syntax transformation; the native ECS mutation statements remain the existing ones. SetBallVelocity snaps the scalar angles at the command boundary. Internal velocity publication does not snap. After the ordered motion step, free non-mushroom old-orientation balls update all nine scalar fields before current_time advances. Formation uses actual loaded offsets, leader rotation and the existing goto thrust/integration. Dynamic orientation, source collision-history correspondence and all interaction variants remain open. Source Stop applies Y damping before collision computation. Original source collision outputs are prepared before Avian damping setup can zero underflowed velocities; the existing publication path then commits them after the App update. DestinyMaxVelocity supplies thrust/input metadata through one ECS component and no longer activates the Avian hard speed cap. An unaligned Warp ball receives the existing source goto thrust after decrementing its alignment stamp. A newly activated or proper warp follows the existing proper-warp selection. Activation events and the complete transition family remain open. Generated position/radius/max-speed/lifecycle adapters update persistent ownership immediately. Motion updates ownership after source angle state at the source displacement threshold; further dynamic/controller phase equivalence remains open. Client evolution retains uninitialized source bubble IDs. Source collision kernels accept arbitrary numeric labels; the Avian extension reads current master/client policy through a derived schedule cache. Source client proximity timers/candidates/events run without initialized bubble labels; full master liveness and geometric candidate correspondence remain open.
views.name: Runtime and scheduling view

views.description: DestinyBallId and runtime ID/entity maps separate stable IDs from Bevy entity identity. Avian f64 Position/Rotation and Destiny metadata carry native state. The generated geometry adapter copies three f64 lanes into the existing Vec3 value type. Snapshot v3 is logical-authoritative JSON; original private binary bytes, solver transients and complete pending-state future equivalence remain gaps. Nine angular/history f64 fields have a single owner in DestinyBallMetadata. Their snapshot representation stores u64 bit patterns, including nonfinite values and signed zero. Roll parameters are park inputs and survive restore. Twelve subsequent steps agree after restore in the scoped integration test. Older snapshot reconstruction and complete history/event equivalence remain open. DestinyMaxVelocity is the single maximum-velocity parameter owner, including checkpoint, snapshot, getter/setter and optional replication paths. Existing API storage is f64 and source motion kernels narrow to f32; complete source API rounding correspondence remains open. The existing Tracking resource owns partition boxes, placements, parent lifetime and source counter. Logical full snapshots retain exact stored ownership, including stale placement and explicitly undefined cast-domain extensions; partial/static/history correspondence remains open.
views.name: State and data view

views.description: The current engine builds as rlib/staticlib/cdylib with --no-default-features and no Blue runtime. Direct Rust tests exercise real Bevy worlds and formation evolution. The existing optional carbon-network feature still compiles, but original Blue/Blueexposure/exefile hosting, wheels and authenticated transport are later integration work. Previous Linux ABI/wheel observations predate the angular source change and are historical. The original twelve Windows/macOS presets still require semantic mapping to the core target matrix; no cross-platform completion is claimed.
views.name: Deployment and integration view

views.description: Compiler extraction establishes the scalar expression structure; syntax comparison checks the existing Rust kernel before reuse. Independent original C++ numeric traces check actual native queries. XML is documentation evidence. Kani observations and Verus scope are separate; generated artifacts, fixture passes and oracle agreement do not grant production refinement or universal equivalence. Angular tests compare 1,224 exact field bits from 136 unchanged original C++ transitions. Direct Rust formation scenarios preserve original fixture setup/order/ten-step coordinates and four-decimal comparison. These are host-scoped observations. Core/full reports share one canonical inventory; unknown or mixed core semantics cannot be deferred because Blue is unavailable. Independent unchanged C++ stop/time-factor/integration samples additionally check all six position/velocity lanes in both source collision configurations. The initial fixtures and an exponential-underflow observation exposed distinct cap and phase-order errors before their fixes. The extended unchanged C++ partition oracle covers 80 client Stop environment/mutation/motion states at four timesteps, and source-backed client-label invariance checks exercise both collision modes.
